label: Mishlei (Proverbs) — Part 1 — Chapters 1–10
summary_plain: Mishlei — the Proverbs of Shelomoh son of Dawid, king of Yisra'EL. The fear of YHWH is the beginning of knowledge. Wisdom cries out in the streets. YHWH by wisdom founded the earth. Trust in YHWH with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding. Chapters 8-9 present Wisdom as a person — she was with YHWH before creation, when he marked out the foundations of the earth, she was beside him as a master craftsman.
summary_scholarly: The ACR reads from DSS Proverbs fragments (4QProv-a, 4QProv-b) and the Orit Ge'ez. The personification of Wisdom (Chokmah) in chapters 1-9 has parallels in the Egyptian wisdom tradition — particularly the Instructions of Ptahhotep (c. 2400 BCE) and the Instructions of Amenemope (c. 1200 BCE). The Hebrew wisdom tradition emerges from the same Afro-Asiatic intellectual matrix as the Egyptian tradition. Mishlei 22:17-24:22 corresponds closely to the Instructions of Amenemope — both texts draw from the same ancient African wisdom framework.

key_terms.definition: Hebrew title for the book of Proverbs, meaning sayings or parables; a collection of wisdom literature attributed primarily to Shlomo ben David.

key_terms.term: Fear of YHWH Beginning of Wisdom
key_terms.definition: The foundational principle of Mishlei (1:7 and 9:10): reverence for YHWH is the starting point of all true wisdom and knowledge.
Wisdom personified as a woman calling in the streets in Mishlei chs 1-9; she represents YHWH's own creative and guiding principle, present before creation.
In Mishlei 8:30, Wisdom declares she was beside YHWH as a craftsman/architect at creation; this ancient text is the source the NT later re-shaped into Logos theology.

key_terms.term: Trust in YHWH Not Your Own Understanding
key_terms.definition: Mishlei 3:5-6 urges total reliance on YHWH rather than human reasoning as the path that makes ways straight.
The list in Mishlei 6:16-19: haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands that shed innocent blood, a heart devising wicked plans, feet running to evil, a false witness, one who sows discord among brothers.
The seductive figure contrasted with Lady Wisdom in Mishlei chs 5-7; represents the path of unfaithfulness and destruction, contrasted with Wisdom's invitation to life.
Primary attributed author of Mishlei (1:1; 10:1; 25:1 — the last section noted as copied by Khizkiyahu's men); the book also contains collections from Agur (ch.30) and Lemuel (ch.31).
The Hebrew word for proverb or parable; root means both 'to compare' and 'to rule'; the basic literary unit of Mishlei, typically in two-line parallel or contrasting form.
The genre including Mishlei, Kohelet, Iyov, Ben Sira, and 4QInstruction; characterized by observation of creation, ethical instruction, and the fear-of-YHWH foundation.

faq.question: What does the Hebrew word mashal mean and why is it significant for Mishlei?
faq.answer: Mashal means a comparison, proverb, or parable — it comes from a root meaning both 'to compare' and 'to rule.' Mishlei is built from these short wisdom statements, mostly in two-line forms where the second line parallels, contrasts, or completes the first. The form itself teaches: wisdom is built by noticing how things relate.

faq.question: Who are the different authors attributed sections in Mishlei?
faq.answer: Mishlei is not a single-author book. Sections are attributed to Shlomo ben David (1:1; 10:1; 25:1 — the last noted as copied by Khizkiyahu's men), Agur son of Yaqeh (ch.30), and King Lemuel — words his mother taught him (31:1). The diversity reflects how Hebrew wisdom traditions were gathered and preserved across generations.

faq.question: What is the significance of Wisdom being described as a craftsman beside YHWH at creation in Mishlei 8:30?
faq.answer: Mishlei 8:22-31 is the original text — written centuries before the NT. It presents Wisdom (Khokhmah) as YHWH's companion and craftsman at creation, present and delighting before him. The NT Logos theology (John 1) is a re-shaping of this ancient Hebrew wisdom tradition; the direction runs from Mishlei to NT, not the other way.

faq.question: What are the two women of Mishlei chapters 1-9 and what do they represent?
faq.answer: Lady Wisdom (Khokhmah) and the Strange Woman (Ishah Zarah / Dame Folly) are the two contrasting figures. Wisdom calls from the heights and city gates, inviting the simple to life and understanding. The Strange Woman seduces with smooth words toward paths of death. This contrast structures chs 1-9 as a father's instruction to a son choosing between two ways.

faq.question: What is the relationship between the fear of YHWH and practical wisdom in Mishlei?
faq.answer: The fear of YHWH is not terror but reverent awe and covenant accountability — the starting orientation that makes all other wisdom possible. Mishlei 1:7 and 9:10 both declare it 'the beginning.' This is not piety added onto practical wisdom — it IS the foundation. Without this orientation, what looks like wisdom is just cleverness that leads to destruction.

faq.question: What does Mishlei say about the power of words?
faq.answer: Mishlei gives unusual weight to speech. Mishlei 18:21: 'Death and life are in the power of the tongue.' 12:18: 'There is one whose rash words are like sword thrusts, but the tongue of the wise brings healing.' 15:1: 'A soft answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.' The power to build or destroy through language is a central wisdom concern.

faq.question: What does Mishlei say about the purpose of discipline and correction?
faq.answer: Mishlei frames discipline (musar) as an act of love. 3:11-12: 'Do not despise YHWH's discipline... for YHWH reproves the one he loves, as a father the son in whom he delights.' 13:24: 'Whoever spares the rod hates his son, but he who loves him is diligent to discipline him.' The goal is life and wisdom, not punishment for its own sake.

faq.question: What does Mishlei 8:22-31 teach about the nature of wisdom in creation?
faq.answer: Wisdom in Mishlei 8 declares she was established before the mountains, before the hills, before the earth. She was beside YHWH as a craftsman and was his delight. This positions wisdom not as a human invention but as a property of creation itself — woven into the fabric of reality that YHWH made. To walk in wisdom is to align with the structure of creation.

faq.question: What evidence from Qumran confirms Mishlei's place in the Hebrew covenant tradition?
faq.answer: Fragments of Mishlei were found at Qumran (4QProva and 4QProvb — 4Q102 and 4Q103), confirming the book was part of the community's library. The Qumran community also produced 4QInstruction (4Q415-418), a wisdom text building on Mishlei's foundation while adding eschatological dimensions — demonstrating Mishlei's continuing influence in the pre-Rabbinic covenant tradition.

faq.question: How does the structure of Lady Wisdom's invitation in Mishlei 9:1-6 work?
faq.answer: Lady Wisdom has built her house with seven pillars, prepared a feast, and sends out her servant-women to call from the highest places of the city: 'Come, eat of my bread and drink of the wine I have mixed. Leave your simple ways, and live, and walk in the way of insight.' The seven pillars, the feast, and the public invitation from the heights contrast directly with Dame Folly's stolen water and hidden bread (9:17) — life versus death as a banquet choice.
